description: Declared reasons for UK targets bound at the 2025 calibration period from an older fact without an uprating index (microcosm#1123). Kinds: matched_period, in_year_snapshot, control_rescaled, reviewed_no_index. uk_runtime.uprating_holds refuses an undeclared, expired or stale hold at compile time. A hold is in force only once it carries approved_by and approved_on and its status is approved: the compile refuses the rows of any other entry. Every entry expires two months after its signature, so each is reviewed again by 2026-12-11.

holds.reason: DfE funded early-education take-up counted in the January 2025 census: a count at a date inside the calibration year, not a lagged period.

DfE funded early-education registrations by single year of age and provision counted in the January 2025 census: a count at a date inside the calibration year, not a lagged period. Requested by María on 2026-10-21 with the single-age rows.

DfE funded early-education working parent registrations at 9 to 11 months counted in the January 2025 census: a count at a date inside the calibration year, not a lagged period. Requested by María on 2026-10-22 with the row, which the spring-term measures and its own under-2 take-up let the model carry (microcosm#1338).
Households capped at November 2025 (DWP benefit cap statistics): a point-in-time stock inside the calibration year.
New Style JSA claimants at August 2025: a point-in-time caseload inside the calibration year.
DWP two-child-limit statistics count open claims in April 2025: a point-in-time population inside the calibration year.
Council-tax dwelling stock at the taxbase dates (England October 2025, Scotland September 2025): stocks counted inside the calibration year.

The CGT rows are HMRC CGT statistics for tax year 2024-25, the latest outturn (27 August 2026); the binding measures them under the 2024-25 rules (measurement_period 2024, require_matching_fact_period). 2024-25 includes disposals brought forward ahead of the October 2024 rate change, so it is not projected forward; 2025-26 outturn is expected around August 2027.

ONS Consumer Trends road fuel (COICOP 07.2.2) for calendar 2024, measured on the frame's own 2024 petrol and diesel columns (measurement_period 2024, require_matching_fact_period). The fact and the stored columns are the same year, so the row does not depend on the engine's 2024-to-2025 fuel projection; measuring the calendar-2025 figure through the engine would put that projection into the weights (microcosm#1324).

OBR's FY2024-25 alcohol, tobacco and betting and gaming receipts, measured on the engine's 2024 duty from the frame's stored FY2024-25 quantities and bases (measurement_period 2024, require_matching_fact_period). policyengine-uk charges model year 2024 at the FY2024-25 rates and holds the excise inputs flat after it (PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk#2596), so measuring a later year would read the engine's projection, not the data (microcosm#1359).

Public transport support and revenue lines for financial year 2024-25, the latest outturn of each publisher (DfT BUS05 and ORR next in November 2026). Spending is set by policy, so no price or volume index carries it forward; held to outturn until the next edition. The England fare-receipts rows are the exception, carried by the BUS0415 fares index. Each binding declares the frame's period (measurement_period 2024), so the outturn is measured on the frame's own columns rather than on the engine's 2025 values (microcosm#1324).
Council-tax dwelling stock by authority at the taxbase dates (England October 2025, Scotland September 2025): stocks counted inside the calibration year.

Census 2021 (Scotland 2022) household cells: their level is set by each nation's 2025 household estimate through the nation and region bridge (microcosm#1123, nations win), so only their census shares within a leg are held.

Census 2021 (Scotland 2022) tenure cells whose share no series drifts: every Welsh, Scottish and Northern Irish authority (the feed pairs no dwelling stock by tenure with their census) and any English authority whose SPREE share moves by more than 10% in two years (a stock reclassification: Rushmoor). Their level follows the authority's household reconciliation through the tenure partition, so only the census share is held. The other English cells are drifted by SPREE and are not holds.

SPI 2023-24 higher rate taxpayer cells by constituency and local authority (England, Wales and Northern Ireland): their level is set by each region's and nation's Table 2.2 row for calendar 2025 through the per-geography bridge, so only their 2023-24 shares within a region or nation are held. The 2024-25 area tables are due early 2027.

HMRC Table 6.2's 2024-25 salary-sacrifice income-tax and employee NICs reliefs, the latest edition. They follow the employer NICs relief row (microcosm#1069 c11), which anchors the sacrificed amount at its 2024-25 level and restates only the rate it is relieved at; the income tax rates and the employee Class 1 main rate (8%) are unchanged from 2024-25 to 2025-26, so no restatement applies. Growing all the reliefs with earnings instead is an open ruling (raised on microcosm#1123, tracked on microcosm#1278 since it closed into it).
ISC census pupil total counted on Census Day, 16 January 2025: a count at a date inside the calibration year, not a lagged period (the January 2026 census falls after it).

SLC student support for higher education in England, academic year 2024/25, the latest final edition of these products. The provisional 2025/26 early-year tables (in the feed) report support totals by level and domicile, not maintenance loans, Parents' Learning Allowance or Adult Dependants' Grant, so they cannot carry these rows; the final 2025/26 edition is due 26 November 2026.

The cars share of fuel duty comes from the OBR's April 2024 note (FY2024-25). HMRC's provisional FY2025-26 fuel duty total is in the feed, but carrying the cars line to calendar 2025 needs a fiscal-to-calendar roll-forward of the total that is not built yet; held to FY2024-25 until it is (a #1123 follow-up, tracked on microcosm#1278 since #1123 closed into it).

Local authority age cells bind ONS mid-2025; constituency cells stay at mid-2024 (England and Wales, NRS's revised 2022-data-zone edition for Scotland) because no mid-2025 constituency edition is published yet (England and Wales due December 2026 to January 2027). Their level is set by the mid-2025 region-tier age controls through the age bridges, so only their shares within a leg are held.

DfT BUS01a local bus passenger journeys for FY2024-25, the latest outturn (DfT's closing-year label fy2025). The binding measures the frame's NTS trips at the boardings per trip the lcfs stage priced from the same FY2024-25 boardings, so both sides are FY2024-25 on purpose; journeys are volumes with no published index (microcosm#1207).

DESNZ sub-national domestic consumption for 2024 (electricity: non-half-hourly meters read 31 January 2024 to 30 January 2025 and half-hourly meters over calendar 2024, both counted, as reported; gas: mid-May 2024 to mid-May 2025, weather-corrected), levelled onto the lcfs stage's calendar-2024 Energy Trends level. The binding measures the frame's stored calendar-2024 spend turned back into kWh at the stage's prices, so both sides are 2024 on purpose; Energy Trends 2025 was weighed as an index and not taken, so the weights do not absorb the change in use per household (microcosm#1207).

Census 2021 (Scotland 2022) households times DESNZ's 2024 gas-to-electricity meter share. The level follows the area's household reconciliation through the census partition (census_gas_connected_share), so only the meter share is held at 2024 (microcosm#1207; re-worded 2026-10-26 by juaristi22 for the constituency grain, microcosm#1095).

SLC Student loan forecasts for England, Table 6a: borrowers liable to repay and earning above the repayment threshold in academic year 2024/25, the stock whose reference date falls inside the calibration year 2025, which Chronicle stores under the academic year's opening year 2024. A stock at a date inside the calibration year, not a lagged period; the student_loans stage tops up to the same stock.

England's dwellings entitled to the single adult household 25% discount at the taxbase date (MHCLG Council Taxbase line 8, October 2025): a stock counted inside the calibration year, as the band rows' are (microcosm#953).

England's dwellings entitled to the single adult household 25% discount by billing authority at the taxbase date (MHCLG Council Taxbase line 8, all bands; the feed labels the count 2025-10): a stock counted inside the calibration year, as the national row's and the band cells' are (microcosm#1095).

HMRC Child Benefit families in payment by number of children at the August 2025 count (Child Benefit Statistics, Annual Release, Table 2): a stock counted inside the calibration year, as the benefit cap's November count is (microcosm#1095).
